themes_detail.label: Encampment surge in Coney Island
themes_detail.summary: Homelessness encampments spiked to 11 complaints THIS WEEK compared to 1.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks—a 780% increase (z-score: 7.0)—suggesting rapid deterioration of street conditions and potential public health/safety crisis in the district.
evidence: 11 encampment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
780% spike with z-score of 7.0 (statistically significant high-severity anomaly)
Suggests acute homelessness crisis emerging in real time in CD 313
reporting_angles: On-the-ground reporting: Where are encampments clustering (Coney Island boardwalk, residential streets, parks)? What services exist?
City response: Why the sudden surge? Is this seasonal, or connected to shelter closures or policy shifts elsewhere in NYC?

themes_detail.label: Drinking-in-public complaints explode
themes_detail.summary: Public drinking complaints hit 4 THIS WEEK versus 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks—a 3100% spike (z-score: 11.72)—indicating a potential clustering of alcohol-related disorder or enforcement sweep in beach/boardwalk areas.
evidence: 4 drinking complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
3100% spike with z-score of 11.72 (highest statistical anomaly in dataset)
Concentrated emergence suggests either behavioral clustering or targeted enforcement action
reporting_angles: Is NYPD conducting summertime boardwalk enforcement sweeps? Interview precinct commanders.
Beach venue angle: Are new bars, open-container sales, or late-night establishments contributing to spike?

themes_detail.label: Street infrastructure damage accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Damaged street signs jumped to 5 complaints THIS WEEK versus 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks—a 900% spike (z-score: 6.36)—alongside concurrent spikes in curb condition (3 complaints last week vs. 0.4 avg) and obstruction complaints (4 THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 avg), suggesting coordinated street degradation or deferred maintenance.
evidence: 5 damaged street sign complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (900% spike, z-score: 6.36)
Curb condition: 3 complaints last week vs. 0.4 average (700% spike)
Obstruction: 4 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 average (1500% spike, z-score: 8.66)
Pattern suggests systemic street infrastructure crisis, not isolated complaints
reporting_angles: Infrastructure audit: Inspect Coney Island/Brighton Beach streets for signs of deferred maintenance. Map complaint clusters.
City budget angle: Is the district underfunded for street maintenance? Review DOE/DOHMH maintenance contracts.

themes_detail.label: Vendor enforcement complaints spike
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints reached 4 last week versus 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks—a 3100% spike (z-score: 11.72)—potentially indicating either aggressive city crackdowns on street vending or emergence of illicit vending operations on boardwalk or commercial strips.
evidence: 4 vendor enforcement complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
3100% spike with z-score of 11.72 (tied for highest anomaly in dataset)
Pattern suggests either coordinated enforcement action or rapid emergence of unlicensed vending
reporting_angles: City enforcement angle: Is DOHMH or Sheriff's Office conducting summertime vendor sweeps on the boardwalk?
Small business angle: Are street vendors facing new regulations or displaced from other districts? Interview vendor associations.

themes_detail.label: Dead animal removal backlog
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints spiked to 7 three weeks ago versus 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks—a 700% spike (z-score: 5.82)—suggesting sanitation or pest control delays during warmer months that may signal broader neighborhood cleanliness issues.
evidence: 7 dead animal complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike, z-score: 5.82)
Timing suggests seasonal surge (summer heat, rodent/pest activity)
Concurrent dumpster complaints (3 vs. 0.4 avg) reinforce sanitation stress
reporting_angles: Sanitation audit: Interview DSNY about response times and rodent control in CD 313. Is there a capacity issue?
Seasonal trend angle: Are summer months historically problematic for street cleanliness in Coney Island?
